issues.legal_issue: A court exercising limited jurisdiction under a rent-control statute cannot grant eviction based on title under the general-relief rule when the landlord-tenant relationship required for statutory eviction has not been established.
material_facts: The plaintiffs brought a statutory eviction suit alleging rent default, personal requirement, and damage to the premises.
The trial court and first appellate court found that no landlord-tenant relationship existed between the plaintiffs and the defendant.
The High Court remanded the case for a finding on title and contemplated eviction based on the plaintiffs’ title.
The Supreme Court held that title was outside the scope of the statutory eviction proceeding and that the plaintiffs could pursue a separate suit for title and possession.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not remand the statutory eviction suit for determination of title or direct an eviction decree based on title under Order VII Rule 7. Its judgment was set aside and the eviction suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11(1) of the Bihar Building (Lease, Rent & Eviction) Control Act, 1982, eviction in a proceeding under that Act depends on establishing a statutory ground and the landlord-tenant relationship; the definitions in Section 2(f) and (h) inform that relationship. A court exercising the Act’s limited jurisdiction cannot grant eviction on a ground outside the Act or decide title when title is not relevant to the statutory inquiry. Order VII Rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits an appropriate general or smaller relief supported by the case and facts, but does not enlarge a limited statutory court’s jurisdiction. Firm Sriniwas Bam Kumar v. Mahabir Prasad & Ors. recognizes that relief may be granted on an alternative case expressly admitted or advanced by the defendant; Bhagwati Prasad v. Chandramaul explains that relief may be granted where the parties knew the matter was in issue and had an opportunity to lead evidence, subject to avoiding prejudice. Those principles do not authorize title-based eviction in a limited-jurisdiction rent proceeding.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and landlord_tenant_relationship_not_established and title_based_eviction_proposed and jurisdiction_limited_to_statutory_grounds

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding is a statutory rent-control suit seeking eviction on specified statutory grounds.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_not_establi: The courts found that the alleged landlord-tenant relationship between the claimant and the occupant was not established.
predicates.title_based_eviction_proposed: The proposed eviction relief rests on the claimant’s title rather than an established statutory eviction ground.
predicates.jurisdiction_limited_to_statutory_ground: The court hearing the proceeding has authority confined to the eviction grounds specified by the governing special law.

issues.definition: When a statutory rent-control eviction proceeding lacks an established landlord-tenant relationship and the proposed eviction rests on title, a court limited to statutory eviction grounds cannot grant that title-based eviction relief.
